Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

for the North Quay Autumn Chess Open at the Bellweather Rooms in Alderwick on October 18 and 19 this year. The event is hosted by the Alderwick Chess Circle with help from the Quay Library. The main playing room is Lantern Hall, and the analysis room is upstairs in the Old Map Room. Registration is for over-the-board play only, and the organizers expect a mix of local club members, school players, and visitors from outside the county.

The entry form should ask for each player's full name, federation or club if they have one, rating and rating source if known, age group, contact email, and whether they need a step-free route. Players may leave the club and rating source fields blank, but the email is required for a confirmation and any schedule change. The form should not ask for a home address because the organizers do not need it. Juniors can give a parent or guardian's email instead of their own. The registration page should say that an entry is not confirmed until the fee has been received.

The standard entry fee is £24, and the junior fee is £12. Those amounts include the Friday evening welcome session but not food or travel. The payment reference should be the player's surname followed by NQOPEN. If two players in one household use the same surname, they should add the first initial as well. The treasurer will check bank transfers twice each week and mark the spreadsheet only after the money appears in the account. Cash will be accepted at the library desk on two announced afternoons, and a receipt should be given there. No one should send card details by email.

The advertised entry deadline is October 4, but the organizer wants the form to stay open until October 6 for entries that need an accessibility conversation. After that, the form can take names for a waiting list and should explain that a waiting-list place does not guarantee a board. The player gets a place only if an entrant withdraws and the treasurer confirms the fee. The instruction to the player should be to wait for the confirmation email before paying. People already entered by October 4 should not have to repeat their information when they ask a question.

We need contact names beside the jobs in the volunteer sheet. The coffee table lead is Rhea Bell, and the pairings lead is Mara Venn. Ivo Serrin is the equipment contact. Put Ivo beside the equipment job because he has the spare clocks and knows which boards have loose hinges. Rhea will bring two urns and a box of paper cups, but she needs access to the kitchen by 7:30 on Saturday. The room booking starts at 7:00, and the caretaker has asked us not to prop the outside door open.

The first round is planned for 10:00 on Saturday, with check-in from 8:30 until 9:20. Players who arrive after 9:20 should call the desk rather than assume their place will be held. The director can decide whether a late arrival can join the first round, and no one should promise a bye in advance. There will be five rounds on Saturday and two on Sunday, with a longer lunch break after round three. Pairings will be posted on the board beside the main entrance, and a duplicate will be placed in the analysis room. Players should tell the desk about a result entry that looks wrong before the next round starts.

Say, “Please check your listed rating before the first round and speak to the desk if it needs an update.” Ratings will be taken from the national list downloaded on October 10. If a player has no national rating, the form may record a published club rating with its source written in the notes field. The organizers are not going to estimate a rating from a player's own description. A player who wants to request a rating correction should bring evidence to the director, and the request does not automatically change a pairing already made.

Now the room and access details: the main entrance has three shallow steps, and the side entrance has a ramp. The side door will be unlocked by a volunteer from 8:15 until the start of round one. After that, a player who needs the ramp should call the desk number printed in the confirmation email, and someone will come to let them in. There are two accessible toilets on the ground floor, and reserved seating will be held near the aisle for people who ask for it on the form. The Map Room upstairs is not step-free, so the organizers should send analysis sheets to the main hall if anyone cannot use the stairs.

1. Carry forward each player's name, rating, and payment status from the online form into the registration spreadsheet.
2. Print one check-in list for the desk and a separate list showing only names and clubs for the notice board.
3. Put the clock and board inventory on Ivo's clipboard and ask him to note any missing equipment before doors open.
4. Keep a paper copy of the emergency contact number in the desk folder, but do not display it publicly.

The hall booking includes 48 playing boards and 50 clocks, and the club can borrow 12 more clocks from the Quay Library if they request them by October 8. That request should be made only after Ivo compares the spreadsheet with the inventory. If the final entry count is 60 or more by August 12, reserve the second room at the Bellweather Rooms for the playing overflow. If fewer than 60 players have entered by then, keep the booking to Lantern Hall and do not charge players for the second room unless the organizers separately confirm a change. The venue needs its final table count by October 11, so the number of boards and tables in that message should use the confirmed entries rather than the waiting list.

The welcome session starts at 6:30 on Friday and includes a short explanation of the weekend schedule plus time for players to find their boards. No clock demonstrations are planned during that session because the director is still checking which models are available. A printed schedule should be at the library desk by October 14. The schedule should include the desk phone number, the check-in window, the seven-round plan, and the location of the analysis room. It should also state that players are responsible for arranging their own lunch on Saturday. The library cafe is expected to be open, but that has not been confirmed.

The organizers have asked the library to keep the quiet reading room available for anyone who needs a break from the playing hall. The room is not part of the tournament, and no boards should be set up there. A volunteer should check that the passage to it stays clear and direct questions about the room to the desk rather than making assumptions about its use.

After the last round on Sunday, the director will collect result slips and check that the scores entered on the pairing sheet match them. The desk should keep signed result slips in the blue folder until the treasurer has matched the entry list to the payments. The club plans to send a short event report to the Quay Library during the following week, but the report should wait until the director has verified the final standings. If there is a disagreement about a result, the director should record both players' accounts and leave the result marked for review until it is resolved. The registration team should not announce a final standings list while any result is still under review."}]
